info.title: Elody GraphQL Service API
info.description:
The HTTP endpoints of a client's GraphQL service, the Node/Express app that serves the PWA. Most of the work goes through `POST /api/graphql`; the other endpoints cover what doesn't fit in a GraphQL response: logging in, files, exports and the PWA's boot config. See [Proxy Endpoints](/services/elody-frontend/proxy-endpoints) for how they work.

The endpoints come from **base-graphql**, except those tagged as added by **mediafileModule**, which every DAMS client installs. A client can add its own endpoints, so check your deployment for extras. The examples use [the garage network](/example-domain).

**Authentication.** These endpoints are meant for the PWA. They use the `connect.sid` session cookie that `POST /api/auth_code` sets, and call collection-api with the token held in the session. A request without a session usually fails with `500 AUTH | NO VALID TOKEN`, unless the deployment allows anonymous users or whitelists the caller's IP or domain. To integrate from another service, call [collection-api](/services/elody-collection/api-reference) directly instead.

**Left out:** `/api/prom/query_range`, which returns fixed sample data.

servers.description: A client's dashboard; the GraphQL service and the PWA share one origin.

post.description:
The Apollo Server endpoint the PWA talks to. The path is `APOLLO_GRAPHQL_PATH`, `/api/graphql` by default.

The schema depends on the modules a client installs, so it isn't listed here. See [GraphQL Modules](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules), or run an introspection query against your own deployment.

**Content-Type must be exactly `application/json`.** Anything else, including `application/json; charset=utf-8`, gets `415 Unsupported Media Type`.

Without a session, queries still run; `extensions.authStatus` in the response is then `UNAUTHENTICATED`.

parameters.name: X-tenant-id
parameters.description: The tenant (garage) to work in. Passed on to collection-api.

parameters.name: X-Parent-Entity-Id
parameters.description: The entity the current page is about. Permission checks that use `$parentEntityId` read it from here.

example.query: query getEntityById($id: String!, $type: String!) { Entity(id: $id, type: $type) { id type intialValues { licence_plate: keyValue(key: "licence_plate", source: metadata) } } }

200.description: The GraphQL result. Errors are reported in `errors` with a 200 status, as GraphQL does.

post.summary: Exchange an authorization code for a session
post.description:
The last step of the OIDC login. The PWA sends the code it received from Keycloak; the server exchanges it for tokens and keeps them in the session. The browser only ever gets the `connect.sid` cookie.

If the session already holds a token that hasn't expired, nothing is exchanged. See [Auth & Session](/services/elody-frontend/auth-session).

200.description: A session now holds valid tokens. Sets the `connect.sid` cookie.

text/plain.example: Something went wrong. Error: AUTHENTICATE | Invalid response from OpenID server: {"error":"invalid_grant"}

get.description: Revokes the session's tokens at Keycloak, destroys the session and clears the `connect.sid` cookie.

500.description: The session could not be destroyed.

get.description: Returns the claims of the session's access token, decoded. Nothing is fetched from Keycloak.

401.description: No session, or the session holds no token.

get.description:
Everything the PWA needs before it can render: OIDC settings, feature flags, routes, translations and the type→URL mapping. The PWA fetches it once at boot.

Some of it is resolved for the user making the request:

- A module feature that names a permission, such as `savedSearch`, is `enabled: false` for a user who fails that permission.
- `features.simpleSearch.itemTypes` only lists the types the user may read.
- Routes with `meta.can` get `meta.permitted`, and routes with `meta.landingRedirect` get `meta.landingRoute`.

Because it is fetched once, a permission change only shows up after a reload.

200.description: The configuration. Served without a `Content-Type` header.

post.description:
Exports the given entities as CSV. Pass `ids`, or pass `parentId` and `relation` to export everything the parent relates to with that relation type.

When the CSV export service is enabled (`api.csvExportService.csvExportServiceEnabled`), it builds the file. Otherwise collection-api does, which needs collection-api's `export` feature.

byRelation.summary: The parts used on a work order

4XX.description: An error from the upstream service, passed on with its status.

500.description: Anything else, including a request without a valid session.

post.description: Asks collection-api for an `.xlsx` of the given entities, or of the first `limit` entities of `type` when `ids` is empty. Needs collection-api's `export` feature. The request may take up to ten minutes.

4XX.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

500.description: Anything else, including a request without a valid session.

post.summary: Download the order of an entity's children
post.description:
Downloads, as CSV, the order of the entities under `parentId`. Edit it and send it back with `POST /api/upload/csv`.

**Needs a client route.** This endpoint proxies to `GET /entities/{id}/order` on collection-api. That route is not part of the base collection-api, so it only works for a client whose collection module adds it.

default.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

post.summary: Upload a new order for an entity's children
post.description:
Sends an edited order CSV, as downloaded from `POST /api/download/csv`, back to collection-api.

**Needs a client route.** This endpoint proxies to `POST /entities/{id}/order` on collection-api. That route is not part of the base collection-api, so it only works for a client whose collection module adds it.

200.description: The order was saved. The body is empty.

default.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

post.description:
Passes an XML file on to collection-api's MARC21 batch import.

**Needs a client route.** This endpoint proxies to `POST /marc21/v1/batch` on collection-api. That route is not part of the base collection-api, so it only works for a client whose collection module adds it.

default.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

post.summary: Import entities and mediafiles from a CSV or Excel file
post.description:
Sends a CSV or `.xlsx` file to collection-api's `POST /batch`. Run it with `dry_run=1` first to validate the file without creating anything. A real run returns the created entities and one upload URL per file the sheet mentions; the PWA then uploads each file to its URL.

Needs collection-api's `import` feature.

Added by [mediafileModule](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules#mediafilemodule).

parameters.name: main_job_id
parameters.description: Job to attach this import to.

200.description: For a dry run, collection-api's validation result. Otherwise the created entities and upload URLs.

default.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

post.summary: Create a mediafile and get its upload URL
post.description:
Creates a mediafile record and returns the URL to upload the file to. With `hasRelation` and `entityId` the mediafile is attached to that entity; without them a new entity of `type` is created with the mediafile.

Leave out `filename` to create a mediafile that only carries metadata, such as an external URL. No upload URL is returned then.

Added by [mediafileModule](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules#mediafilemodule).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the new entity when there's no `hasRelation`. Defaults to `customization.uploadEntityTypeToCreate`, then `BaseEntity`.

200.description: The upload URL, as a JSON string.

default.description: An error from collection-api, passed on with its status.

get.description:
Looks up the mediafile's download URLs on collection-api and streams the file. By default that's the transcode (the web-friendly version); pass `original=true` for the uploaded file.

Needs a client policy that gives the user `copyright_access`, as collection-api's `download-urls` does.

Added by [mediafileModule](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules#mediafilemodule).

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The mediafile id. The last path segment is used as the id.

parameters.name: originalFilename
parameters.description: Download as an attachment with this name. The extension is taken from the content type.

500.description: Any failure, as an HTML error page.

get.summary: Download an entity's files as a zip
get.description:
Asks the transcode service to build a zip for the entity and streams it back. Needs the transcode service.

Added by [mediafileModule](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules#mediafilemodule).

Content-Disposition.description: Passed on from the transcode service.

default.description: An error from the transcode service, passed on with its status.

get.summary: Get an IIIF image or manifest
get.description:
Proxies the IIIF image service (Cantaloupe) for the [media viewers](/services/elody-frontend/features/media-viewers). Tiles, crops and scaled images are streamed as-is.

For paths ending in `.json` (`info.json`, manifests), the `id` in the response is rewritten to an `/api/iiif/…` URL so that viewers request the tiles through this proxy too.

An `Authorization` header on the request is used as-is, for services that call with their own token. Otherwise the session's token is used. Errors are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Added by [mediafileModule](/services/elody-frontend/graphql-modules#mediafilemodule).

200.description: The image, or the JSON document with its `id` rewritten.

default.description: An error from the IIIF service, passed on with its status.

get.description:
Any page URL of the PWA also serves the entity it shows as data, when the `Accept` header asks for an RDF format or JSON. The last path segment is taken as the entity id, and the request is passed on to collection-api's `GET /entities/{id}` with the same `Accept` header.

A browser asking for `text/html` gets the PWA page as usual. See [Linked Open Data](/services/elody-frontend/features/linked-open-data).

This request does **not** use the session. Send an `Authorization` header, or the entity must be readable anonymously.

200.description: The entity in the requested format.

401.description: collection-api needs a token for this entity.

text/plain.example: Could not reach the collection api

get.description: Answers 200 as long as the process is up. It checks no dependencies.

200.description: The service is up. The body is empty.

get.description: The version of the GraphQL service, from the `version` config. A local build reports `development-version`.

get.summary: Get SEO meta tags for a page
get.description:
Renders an HTML snippet with Open Graph meta tags for the entity on `request_uri`, for crawlers and link previews. Title, description and image come from the metadata keys in `features.SEO.seoMetadataKeys`.

Only exists when the `SEO` feature is configured. The entity is fetched with the static token.

404.description: The SEO feature is not configured.

bearerAuth.description: Only where noted: a token passed on as-is.

redirectUri.description: Must match the redirect URI the login started with.

features.description: Base flags, plus one `{ enabled }` entry per feature a module contributes.

translations.description: Base and client translations merged, per language.

type.description: Entity type; picks the collection to export from.

field.description: Metadata keys to put in the columns.

links.description: One upload URL per file, with `parent_job_id` appended.
